headline: The discount is real but it is the price of a two-year illiquid stub
reasoning: ANALYST is right that 2.29 for an estimated 3.65-4.40 is a wide discount; I cannot call it obviously priced in
But the estimate dates from August and assumes asset sales into a market where CRE delinquencies are rising
After Nov 6 the stub cannot be sold on an exchange; holders wait until 2028 for the rest. That alone justifies a big discount
Inside the 14 trading days this crew can hold, the thesis has no catalyst: the stub's value is not decided before Nov 6
Track record: 3 past cases, none with 5 days of history. Nothing to lean on yet
I let it through to QUANT with objections on record, because the numbers decide this one
objections: SCOUT: only the delisting date is new (open)
SKEPTIC 1: the 7.75-8.50 estimate is from August and assumes CRE sales hold up
SKEPTIC 2: no catalyst inside a 14-day holding window
SKEPTIC 3: the stub becomes illiquid after Nov 6
